new_scholarship.name: Gates Cambridge Scholarship
new_scholarship.program_type: Private trust scholarship for international postgraduate students
new_scholarship.description: The Gates Cambridge Trust awards around 70 full-cost scholarships each year to applicants from outside the United Kingdom to pursue a postgraduate degree in any subject available at the University of Cambridge, with approximately two-thirds of awards offered to PhD candidates. A scholarship covers the University Composition Fee, a maintenance allowance of GBP 23,152 for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate, one economy single airfare at both the beginning and end of the course, inbound visa costs and the Immigration Health Surcharge. Applications for entry in the 2027/8 academic year are open, with the funding deadline set by each course as either 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027.
new_scholarship.duration: Full duration of the Cambridge degree; maintenance allowance stated for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate and awarded for up to 4 years for PhD scholars
new_scholarship.deadline: Dependent on course: either Tuesday 8 December 2026 or Wednesday 6 January 2027, full application submitted by 11:59pm UK time
new_scholarship.application_period: Applications for entry in the academic year 2027/8 opened on 11 September 2026 and close by the Course Funding Deadline listed for each programme in the University Course Directory
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Citizens of any country outside the United Kingdom applying to a Cambridge PhD (full-time or part-time), MLitt (full-time), or one-year full-time postgraduate course, excluding a listed set of business, medical and non-standard degrees.
eligibility: A citizen of any country outside the United Kingdom
Applying to a University of Cambridge PhD (full-time or part-time), MLitt (full-time), or one-year full-time postgraduate course, with some exceptions
Part-time study is only eligible for the PhD; Gates Cambridge is continuing to pilot a scheme allowing applicants to apply for funding for a part-time doctoral degree
Current Cambridge students may apply for a new postgraduate course, and current Gates Cambridge Scholars may apply for a second scholarship for a new degree
Students already part way through a PhD cannot apply for a Gates Cambridge Scholarship to fund the remainder of it
coverage: University Composition Fee at the appropriate rate
Maintenance allowance for a single student (GBP 23,152 for 12 months at the 2026-27 rate, pro rata for shorter courses)
One economy single airfare at both the beginning and the end of the course
Inbound visa costs and the cost of the Immigration Health Surcharge
benefits: Full tuition cost at the University of Cambridge
Living cost maintenance allowance
Return economy airfare
Inbound visa and Immigration Health Surcharge costs
Discretionary academic development funding of up to GBP 750 to up to GBP 4,000, dependent on course length, for conferences and courses
Discretionary Dependent Children Allowance of up to GBP 12,793 per annum for one child and up to GBP 18,244 per annum for two or more children; no funding is provided for a partner
Discretionary hardship funding for unforeseen difficulties
Ability to apply to keep the normal maintenance allowance while on fieldwork during a PhD
Maternity and paternity funding: studies may be interrupted for up to 6 months while the maintenance allowance continues

Reasons for choice of course

application_method: Apply through the University of Cambridge postgraduate admissions process by the Course Funding Deadline published for the course in the University Course Directory
All application documents, including references, must be submitted by 11:59pm UK time on the stated date
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Applications are ranked by department after the funding deadline, applicants are notified of the outcome by 11:59pm UK time on Monday 8 March 2027 for the international round, then reviewed and selected by panels on 22-23 March 2027, with scholarships offered by early April 2027.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Applicants from outside the United Kingdom with high academic achievement and a demonstrable social-leadership record who are applying to a Cambridge postgraduate course whose funding deadline falls on 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027.
new_scholarship.notes: Two selection rounds run each year. A separate earlier round applies to US citizens resident in the USA, who must apply in October and are not eligible for the later round; that round opened 11 September 2026 and closed 14 October 2026.
new_scholarship.funding_period: per 12-month maintenance allowance (2026-27 rate); the award is full-cost and also includes tuition, return airfare, visa and Immigration Health Surcharge

new_scholarship.name: Clarendon Fund Scholarship
new_scholarship.description: The Clarendon Fund is the University of Oxford's largest scholarship scheme, awarding over 200 new fully-funded scholarships each year to graduate scholars of outstanding academic merit and potential, with about 700 scholars on course from roughly 70 nations. Scholarships cover course fees in full for both Home and Overseas fee status students and pay an annual living-expense grant for full-time scholars of at least the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate, which was at least GBP 20,780 in 2025-26. There is no separate scholarship application: every applicant to a degree-bearing Master's or DPhil course who applies by the December or January deadline for their course is automatically considered.
new_scholarship.duration: Normally the scholar's period of fee liability for the course; at the discretion of the academic divisions some awards extend beyond the fee liability period, during which only a living-expense grant is paid
new_scholarship.deadline: Course-dependent: the December or January 2027 admissions deadline for the applicant's course, whichever is relevant
new_scholarship.application_period: Open for the 2027/28 graduate cycle; consideration is automatic for applications submitted by each course's December or January 2027 funding deadline
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Any applicant of any nationality or country of ordinary residence applying to start a new full-time or part-time degree-bearing Master's or DPhil course at Oxford by the December or January deadline for that course.
eligibility: Applying to start a new full-time or part-time Master's or DPhil course at the University of Oxford
Submitted the graduate application by the December or January deadline relevant to the course
No restrictions on nationality, country of ordinary residence or field of study
Includes students already studying for a Master's at Oxford who are re-applying for a DPhil or a second Master's course
Excludes applicants holding a deferred graduate offer
Excludes current students continuing the same degree at Oxford in the next year
Postgraduate Certificate and Postgraduate Diploma courses are not eligible
coverage: Full course fees, including college fees, for Home and Overseas fee status students
Annual living-expense grant for full-time scholars of at least the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate
Study support grant for scholars on part-time courses, set at a sixth, a third or half of the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate depending on the course
For modular fee structure part-time courses: the Annual Award Fee for a maximum of two years, the Registration Fee in full and the Dissertation Fee in full

Living-expense grant of at least GBP 20,780 per year for full-time scholars in 2025-26
Study support grant for part-time scholars

Future academic potential and aptitude for the proposed course of study
Student motivation, evidenced through the personal statement and referees' reports
required_documents: Complete Oxford graduate application for the course
application_method: Apply for the relevant Oxford graduate course through the normal admissions process by the December or January deadline for that course

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Departments assess academic merit and suitability and nominate to the division; divisions review nominations in February or March and shortlist the top-ranked departmental nominees; most initial Clarendon offers are sent by the end of April. Unsuccessful applicants are not contacted.

new_scholarship.notes: Awards are normally for the period of fee liability; Oxford's continuation charges are expressly not covered by the Clarendon Fund. Where a division awards extra study beyond fee liability, only the living-expense grant is paid during that period.
new_scholarship.funding_period: per year (2025-26 living-expense grant floor for full-time scholars)

programme_detail_official.description: The Clarendon Fund is Oxford's largest scholarship scheme, awarding over 200 new fully-funded scholarships a year on academic merit and potential alone, with no nationality or subject restrictions. Applicants who hold a deferred graduate offer are not eligible for Clarendon consideration.
Most initial Clarendon offers go out by the end of April; unsuccessful applicants are not contacted, so silence by mid-June means no award.

new_scholarship.name: Gulbenkian Institute for Advanced Study Fellowships 2027/28
new_scholarship.description: The Gulbenkian Institute for Advanced Study in Lisbon awards fellowships to international academics, emeriti, independent scholars and artists for residencies of three to eight months to work on projects of their own choosing. Each fellowship includes travel expenses, travel and health insurance, a monthly stipend and a partial housing allowance. Applications for the 2027/28 cycle are open from 1 July 2026 until 15 October 2026 at 15:00 Lisbon time, and offers are made from late January of the following year.
